FILE2FILE / INSTALLATION & FIRST RUN

From download
to your first file.

Pick your operating system below. Follow the numbered steps, check that each worked, then try one small conversion.

WindowsmacOSLinuxFirst conversionTroubleshooting

File2File is a desktop app. These installers are for computers, not iPhone, iPad, or Android. External engines are separate downloads.

WINDOWS / X64

Windows, one step at a time.

01

Download the right installer

Open Settings → System → About. Under System type, check that you have an x64-based processor. These packages are x64 builds, not native Windows ARM builds.

Download the EXE installer or download the MSI.

02

Check the download

Download SHA256SUMS.txt and keep both files in Downloads. Open PowerShell and run:

Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "$HOME\Downloads\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-File2File_0.2.2_x64-setup.exe"

Compare the hash to the line with the exact same filename in SHA256SUMS.txt. Letter case does not matter. If you chose the MSI, use its filename instead. A mismatch means you should download again before installing.

03

Install File2File

Double-click the EXE or MSI and follow the installer. The package is unsigned. If SmartScreen shows a reputation warning, verify the download first; More info → Run anyway may be available on a personal computer. A school or work policy can prevent this.

Open File2File from the Start menu. Data and archive jobs can work without external engines.

04

Install the conversion engines

Open PowerShell. Run winget --version first. If it is missing, install or update Microsoft App Installer using Microsoft’s WinGet guide.

Run these commands one at a time. Wait for each to finish and respond to its installer prompts:

winget install --source winget --exact --id Gyan.FFmpeg
winget install --source winget --exact --id JohnMacFarlane.Pandoc
winget install --source winget --exact --id ImageMagick.ImageMagick
winget install --source winget --exact --id oschwartz10612.Poppler

Close PowerShell and File2File after installation, then open them again so the updated PATH is picked up.

05

Confirm the engines are available

In a new PowerShell window, run each command:

ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version
pandoc --version
magick --version
pdftotext -v
pdftohtml -v

Each should print its tool name and version. Then open Engine Health in File2File and refresh it. If a command is not recognized, find that engine’s executable folder, add that folder to your user PATH through Edit environment variables for your account → Path → Edit → New, and restart the app. Poppler’s executables may be inside Library\bin in its extracted package. Add the folder containing the EXEs, not the ZIP file.

Continue to your first conversion
MACOS / APPLE SILICON & INTEL

Set up your Mac.

01

Check your Mac and download

Open Apple menu → About This Mac. A Chip entry such as Apple M1, M2, M3, or later means Apple Silicon. An Intel Processor entry means Intel.

Download for Apple Silicon · Download for Intel

02

Check the DMG

Download SHA256SUMS.txt too. Open Terminal and run the command matching your Mac:

shasum -a 256 "$HOME/Downloads/aarch64-apple-darwin-File2File_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg"

For Intel, use:

shasum -a 256 "$HOME/Downloads/x86_64-apple-darwin-File2File_0.2.2_x64.dmg"

Match the result to the exact filename in SHA256SUMS.txt. If it differs, download again.

03

Install and approve the app

Open the DMG and drag File2File into Applications. Eject the disk image, then open the installed app.

v0.2.2 uses ad-hoc signatures and is not Apple notarized. After a blocked launch, System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway may be available. Approve only the verified copy you chose to install. See Apple’s opening instructions.

If the message says the app is damaged, check the checksum and download again; do not assume every damage warning is only a notarization issue. If the problem persists, use the issue tracker and include your Mac architecture and the exact message.

04

Install the engines with Homebrew

Open Terminal and run brew --version. If Homebrew is not installed, follow the official Homebrew installation instructions and complete the “Next steps” printed by the installer. Then run:

brew install ffmpeg imagemagick pandoc poppler

Wait for installation to finish. These packages supply all six engine executables.

05

Check Engine Health

Run the engine version commands:

ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version
pandoc --version
magick --version
pdftotext -v
pdftohtml -v

Close File2File completely, reopen it, and refresh Engine Health. If the commands work in Terminal but the app cannot find them, Finder’s environment may not include Homebrew. Close the app and start the installed executable with Homebrew on its PATH:

file2file_executable=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :CFBundleExecutable" /Applications/File2File.app/Contents/Info.plist)
env PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH" "/Applications/File2File.app/Contents/MacOS/$file2file_executable"

Keep that Terminal window open while using the app. If an engine was found but is unusable, repair that engine rather than adding another copy elsewhere. File2File prioritizes an executable beside the app, then its application-data bin folder, then system PATH.

Continue to your first conversion
LINUX / X64

Choose DEB or AppImage.

01

Check your architecture and choose a package

Open a terminal and run:

uname -m

x86_64 matches the published Linux packages. ARM systems need a separate compatible build.

On Debian, Ubuntu, or a compatible distribution, choose the DEB package. For other supported Linux setups, try the AppImage.

02

Verify the checksum

Download SHA256SUMS.txt into the same folder as the package. In that folder, run the command for the package you chose:

sha256sum x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-File2File_0.2.2_amd64.deb

Or:

sha256sum x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-File2File_0.2.2_amd64.AppImage

Compare it with the matching filename in SHA256SUMS.txt. Use your browser’s actual download folder, which may differ from Downloads.

03

Install the DEB or run the AppImage

DEB: open a terminal in the download folder and run:

sudo apt install ./x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-File2File_0.2.2_amd64.deb

APT resolves the declared dependencies. Launch File2File from your application menu.

AppImage: in the folder containing the file, run:

chmod +x x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-File2File_0.2.2_amd64.AppImage
./x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-File2File_0.2.2_amd64.AppImage

If your system reports a FUSE or shared-library error, install the matching runtime through your distribution’s package manager. The DEB is usually the simpler choice on a compatible distribution.

04

Install engines and confirm readiness

For AppImage users on Debian or Ubuntu:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install ffmpeg imagemagick pandoc poppler-utils

On Arch-based systems, the engine command is:

sudo pacman -S ffmpeg imagemagick pandoc poppler

On other distributions, use their package manager for the same tools. Reopen File2File and refresh Engine Health. ImageMagick 6 may provide convert rather than magick; File2File supports that Unix fallback.

Continue to your first conversion
FIRST RUN / A SMALL TEST

Make your first conversion.

01

Start with a sample

Download this tiny sample CSV. If your browser displays it instead, save it as file2file-sample.csv. Data conversion uses the built-in Rust engine, so it is a useful first test even before installing external engines.

02

Choose JSON and a destination

Open the desktop app and drop in the CSV. Choose JSON as the output format. Keep the default source-folder destination, or select a folder you can write to. Use auto-rename if a previous result already exists.

03

Review and run

Read the readiness check and its warnings, then start conversion. When it finishes, open the output folder and inspect the JSON. You should see the sample names and scores. Conversion changes the representation; it does not simply rename the file.

04

Try the category you actually need

Try a small PNG → WebP, MP4 → MP3, or Markdown → DOCX after its engine is ready. Open the result to check quality. For a mixed batch, the app only offers targets compatible with every selected input.

WHEN SOMETHING STOPS

Find the cause, then retry.

The download link opens a blank tab
Open the GitHub release page directly in your browser and select the file under Assets. If an in-app browser blocks the handoff, open this site in Safari, Chrome, or Firefox.
An output format is unavailable
Check Engine Health. A missing or unusable engine disables affected conversions. If engines are ready, that input/target pair may not be supported.
An engine is “found but unusable”
Run that executable’s version command. Repair or replace it if it fails. A broken app-local engine takes precedence over a working copy on PATH.
The result looks different
PDF extraction may lose layout, fonts, forms, and images. XLSX conversion uses the first worksheet. JPEG flattens transparency to white. Lossy audio and video encoding can reduce quality.
The output already exists or cannot be written
Choose auto-rename, skip, or explicit overwrite. Try a writable output folder. Existing extracted directories are not overwritten.
You need help with a failure
Copy the app’s batch report. Include the app version, operating system, input/output formats, and Engine Health message when reporting an issue. You can describe the file without sharing private contents.
